es: Moderar una mesa redonda de tres voces: dar la bienvenida, presentar el tema, ceder turnos, reconducir con cortesía, resumir las posturas y cerrar agradeciendo.

vocabulary.es: hilar las ideas, resumir en conjunto
abrir el turno de preguntas al público

teaching.en: Let me extend a warm welcome to everyone and introduce tonight's topic: how technology is changing the classroom.
teaching.es: Permítanme dar una cálida bienvenida a todos y presentar el tema de esta noche: cómo la tecnología está cambiando el aula.
teaching.explanationEs: Extend a warm welcome es la fórmula formal de apertura; introduce sirve tanto para personas como para temas.
segments: Let me extend a warm welcome to everyone and
introduce tonight's topic: how technology is changing the classroom.
teaching.audioText: Let me extend a warm welcome to everyone and introduce tonight's topic: how technology is changing the classroom.

teaching.en: Before we begin, I will set the agenda: a quick round of views, one question from the floor, and a closing summary.
teaching.es: Antes de empezar, fijaré el orden del día: una ronda rápida de opiniones, una pregunta del público y un resumen final.
teaching.explanationEs: Set the agenda anuncia la estructura de la sesión, igual que una señal de organización en una charla.
segments: Before we begin, I will set the agenda: a quick round
of views, one question from the floor, and a closing summary.
teaching.audioText: Before we begin, I will set the agenda: a quick round of views, one question from the floor, and a closing summary.

teaching.en: Each panellist will weigh the benefits against the risks, and I will keep the discussion on track if anyone drifts.
teaching.es: Cada ponente sopesará las ventajas frente a los riesgos, y yo mantendré la discusión encauzada si alguien se desvía.
teaching.explanationEs: Weigh the benefits + against indica comparación; keep the discussion on track es la tarea central del moderador.
segments: Each panellist will weigh the benefits against the risks, and
I will keep the discussion on track if anyone drifts.
teaching.audioText: Each panellist will weigh the benefits against the risks, and I will keep the discussion on track if anyone drifts.

teaching.en: Let me draw the threads together: our first panellist stressed the gains, and our second cast doubt on the cost.
teaching.es: Déjenme hilar las ideas: nuestro primer ponente subrayó las ventajas y el segundo puso en duda el costo.
teaching.explanationEs: Draw the threads together resume posturas distintas con verbos variados (stressed, cast doubt on).
segments: Let me draw the threads together: our first panellist stressed
the gains, and our second cast doubt on the cost.
teaching.audioText: Let me draw the threads together: our first panellist stressed the gains, and our second cast doubt on the cost.

teaching.en: Once every panellist has spoken, I will open the floor to questions and then wrap up the session on time.
teaching.es: Cuando cada ponente haya hablado, abriré el turno de preguntas y después cerraré la sesión a tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: Open the floor to questions da la palabra al público; wrap up the session es la señal de cierre.
segments: Once every panellist has spoken, I will open the floor
to questions and then wrap up the session on time.
teaching.audioText: Once every panellist has spoken, I will open the floor to questions and then wrap up the session on time.

teaching.en: To close this round of discussions, I am deeply grateful to each guest for a lively, honest and generous exchange.
teaching.es: Para cerrar esta ronda de debates, estoy profundamente agradecido a cada invitado por un intercambio animado, sincero y generoso.
teaching.explanationEs: Deeply grateful to + persona dirige el agradecimiento; of sería un calco de «agradecido de».
segments: To close this round of discussions, I am deeply grateful
to each guest for a lively, honest and generous exchange.
teaching.audioText: To close this round of discussions, I am deeply grateful to each guest for a lively, honest and generous exchange.

prompt.es: Elige la apertura adecuada de una moderadora que presenta la mesa.

choices.text: Welcome, everyone; tonight's topic is homework, and I will set the agenda in a moment.
Hello. I will now give my own opinion on homework, and then you may comment.
Good evening. Please be quiet while I explain why homework is useless.

feedback.es: Dar la bienvenida, anunciar el tema y fijar el orden del día es lo propio de quien modera; las otras opciones imponen su opinión.

hint.es: La moderadora da la bienvenida y presenta el tema, no su opinión.

prompt.es: Completa: «Déjame presentar a Sara, nuestra primera ponente.»

feedback.es: Introduce es el verbo habitual para presentar a una persona ante un grupo.

hint.es: No es present: es el verbo para presentar a personas.

origin.text: Let me ___ Sara, our first panellist, who has taught science for twenty years.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Empecemos con una ronda breve de opiniones.»

answer.text: Let us begin with a short round of views

feedback.es: Let us begin with… abre la dinámica y a short round of views fija el formato de la sesión.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿cómo cede el turno la moderadora?

choices.text: She gives the turn to Tom and promises Sara an extra minute later.
She gives the turn to Tom and reminds him of the time.
She gives the turn to Tom and asks him to respond to Sara.

feedback.es: Agradece a Ana, cede la palabra a Tom y le recuerda el límite de tres minutos porque Sara también espera.

origin.audio: Thank you, Ana. Tom, I know you see this slightly differently. Please go ahead, but keep in mind that Sara is also waiting, so let us try to stay within three minutes each.

prompt.es: ¿Qué resumen de la moderadora es fiel a ambas posturas?

choices.text: Ana stressed the time saved, while Tom warned that schools would waste money on them.
Ana suggested buying more tablets, while Tom doubted that they saved time.
Ana stressed the time saved, while Tom doubted that schools could pay for them.

feedback.es: Ana subraya el ahorro de tiempo y Tom duda de que los colegios puedan pagarlas; las otras versiones deforman una de las dos posturas.

origin.text: Ana said that tablets saved time in her classes. Tom replied that he doubted that schools could afford enough of them.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el momento de la mesa.

pairs: Let me extend a warm welcome to everyone.
Let me draw the threads together.
I will open the floor to questions now.
I am deeply grateful to each of you.

feedback.es: Cada frase marca una etapa de la mesa: abrir, dar turno, resumir, abrir preguntas o cerrar.

pairs: Let me extend a warm welcome to everyone.
Let me draw the threads together.
I will open the floor to questions now.
I am deeply grateful to each of you.

prompt.es: Modera la mesa: presenta, da dos turnos, resume y cierra.

answer.text: Good evening, everyone, and welcome to tonight's panel. Our topic is technology in the classroom. Let me introduce our three panellists: Ana, who uses tablets every day; Tom, who teaches science; and Sara, who has three children at school. Ana, would you like to start? Thank you, Ana. Tom, it is your turn. Sorry to cut in, Tom, but coming back to the main question, could you pin down the cost? Thank you. Before we move on, let me draw the threads together. Ana stressed that tablets saved time. Tom doubted that schools could afford them, and he warned that screens could distract pupils. Sara suggested that we write clear rules, and she conceded that tablets had real benefits. Sara, what would your first rule be? Seldom have I seen three guests agree on so much. To wrap up, all of you agree that rules matter more than machines. I am deeply grateful to each panellist for a lively discussion, and I thank our audience for listening. Good night, everyone.

Tom, it is your turn. Sorry to cut in, Tom, but coming back to the main question, could you pin down the cost? Thank you. Before we move on, let me draw the threads together. Ana stressed that tablets saved time. Tom doubted that schools could afford them, and he warned that screens could distract pupils. Sara suggested that we write clear rules, and she conceded that tablets had real benefits. Sara, what would your first rule be? Seldom have I seen three guests agree on so much. To wrap up, all of you agree that rules matter more than machines. I am deeply grateful to each panellist for a lively discussion, and I thank our audience for listening. Good night, everyone.

Welcome, everyone, to our panel. Tonight's topic is technology in the school, and I would like to introduce Ana, Tom and Sara. Ana, please start us off. Thank you. Tom, over to you. Coming back to the topic, could you explain the cost of a class set? Thank you, Tom. Let me recap what we have heard. Ana stressed that tablets saved time. Tom doubted that schools could pay for them. Sara suggested that we make clear rules, and she admitted that tablets helped her own pupils. Is that a fair summary? Good. Sara, what would your first rule be? Sorry to cut in, Tom, but I think that Sara wants to add one short point about homework. Sara, please go ahead. To sum up, everybody agrees that rules matter. I am grateful to each panellist for this lively discussion. Good night, and thank you all for listening. It was a real pleasure to lead this discussion.

feedback.es: Una buena moderación presenta, cede turnos, reconduce, resume con verbos precisos y cierra agradeciendo.

origin.text: Mesa redonda de tres voces sobre tecnología en el aula (Ana a favor, Tom con dudas sobre el costo, Sara pide normas). Escribe en inglés lo que dirías como moderadora (170–250 palabras): da la bienvenida y presenta el tema y a los ponentes; cede dos turnos; reconduce con cortesía; resume cada postura con verbos variados (stressed, doubted, suggested…); y cierra agradeciendo.

evidenceGroups: i would like to hear from

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué condición pone Tom para apoyar las tablets?

choices.text: That the authorities make the true figures public.
That schools limit them to a few classrooms.
That the pupils help to write the rules.

feedback.es: Tom asintió al resumen, pero añadió que las apoyaría si el municipio publicara los costos reales.

origin.audio: Near the end of the panel, the moderator summed up: Ana stressed that tablets save time, Tom doubted that schools can afford them, and Sara suggested writing clear rules. Then she asked whether that was a fair summary. Tom nodded, but added that he would support tablets if the council published the real costs. Ana said that she could live with that, and Sara reminded everyone that rules cost nothing. The moderator smiled, thanked all three, and said that, for once, a panel on technology had ended with a plan instead of a quarrel.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué da a entender el comentario final de la moderadora?

choices.text: That panels on technology are usually too short to matter.
That this panel achieved more than such panels usually do.
That the guests avoided discussing their real disagreements.

feedback.es: «For once» sugiere que lo habitual es terminar en disputa: valora que esta mesa acabara con un plan.

Then she asked whether that was a fair summary. Tom nodded, but added that he would support tablets if the council published the real costs. Ana said that she could live with that, and Sara reminded everyone that rules cost nothing. The moderator smiled, thanked all three, and said that, for once, a panel on technology had ended with a plan instead of a quarrel.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su tarea era mantener la discusión encauzada y ser justa con todos.»

feedback.es: Keep the discussion on track es la colocación que describe la tarea central de quien modera.

origin.text: The moderator did not give her own opinion. Her job was to ___ the discussion on track and to give every panellist a fair hearing.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Estoy profundamente agradecido a cada ponente por la discusión de esta noche.»

answer.text: I am deeply grateful to each panellist for tonight's discussion

feedback.es: Deeply grateful to + persona dirige el agradecimiento, y for + sustantivo indica el motivo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender el autor sobre los resúmenes descuidados?

choices.text: That they tend to give too much time to the guest who spoke last.
That guests rarely notice any real difference between the two versions.
That they may soften a guest's position to please the room.

feedback.es: Advierte que un resumen debe ser fiel aunque incomode: sugiere que el descuido tiende a suavizar la postura de alguien para agradar.

origin.text: A summary is not a vote. When a moderator draws the threads together, she must not choose the most comfortable version of what each guest said. If Sara doubted the plan, the summary says that she doubted it, even if the room would prefer to hear that she had merely asked a question.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué valora más la moderadora al cerrar?

choices.text: The polite way in which the guests disagreed.
The passion with which the guests defended their views.
The number of people who came to the session.

feedback.es: Da las gracias sobre todo a los ponentes «who disagreed with great courtesy»: valora la cortesía en el desacuerdo.

origin.audio: Our time is up. Thank you for coming, and thank you most of all to our panellists, who disagreed with great courtesy, which is rarer than people think.
